title: だって, だから and それから
summary: だって is だ plus って, "it is said": it accepts what came before and then reports, argues or gives an example. だから and それから are built the same way, from だ and から.

blocks.text: Dictionaries list many meanings for **だって**: because, but, even, "I hear". They all come from one idea once you see the parts.

**だ** is the copula, and it points back at what was just said: "that is so" (like the そう in そうですね). **って** is a casual shortening of the quotation particle と plus いう ("say"). Together: "it is said that so".
明日は晴れだって。 They say tomorrow will be sunny.

blocks.en: They say tomorrow will be rainy.

blocks.text: At the start of a reply, だって works like a child's protest. The speaker **accepts** the other person's statement and then adds something that pushes back. That is why it can mean "but..." or "because...": both accept the first line and add a second.

lines.jp: このケーキ、おいしいね。
lines.en: This cake is delicious, isn't it?

lines.jp: だって、さくらが作ったから。
だって、時間がなかった。

blocks.text: Attached to one noun, だって means "even": "take the case of me". It has a casual, slightly defensive tone, unlike the neutral も.

rows: Even I can do it (a bit defensive)

blocks.jp: 子供だって知っている。

blocks.text: だから and それから

**だから** is a short form of "since that is so": だ points back at what was said, and **から** originally means "from", so "from that, this follows". **それから** is also "from that", but in time: **after that**. It does **not** mean "because of that".

blocks.en: It is raining, so I am staying home.

blocks.jp: ご飯を食べて、それから寝た。
blocks.en: I ate, and after that I went to bed.

items: A reply starting with だって accepts, then pushes back: "but / because".
**だから**: so; **それから**: after that (not "because").

options: They say it will snow next week
questions.note: だ + って: it is said.
questions.en: They say it will be snowy next week.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap: accept, then protest
questions.prompt: A：もう寝なさい。　B：＿＿、まだ眠くない。
questions.note: A reply starting with だって accepts and pushes back.
questions.en: A: Go to bed now. B: But I am not sleepy yet.

questions.note: だから: since that is so.
questions.en: It is raining today. So I will stay home.

questions.prompt: 朝ご飯を食べた。＿＿、学校へ行った。
questions.note: それから: after that, in time.
questions.en: I ate breakfast. After that, I went to school.

questions.prompt: 私＿＿、そんなことはできない。
questions.note: Noun + だって: even.

questions.prompt: 友達は来週日本へ行く＿＿。
questions.note: A casual って at the end reports what you heard.
questions.en: I hear my friend is going to Japan next week.

questions.instruction: Which two parts make だって?
questions.note: だ points back at what was said; って is the casual quote.

questions.instruction: Which word is the second part of だから?
questions.note: "From that, this follows."

questions.instruction: What does それから add?
questions.prompt: 宿題をして、それからゲームをした。
questions.note: それから: from that, in time.
questions.en: I did my homework, and after that I played a game.

questions.instruction: Which reply accepts what was said and then pushes back?
options: それから、行きたくない。
questions.note: だって starts a protest: "but / because".
questions.en: A: Tomorrow is a school day. B: ...

questions.instruction: What does だって mean here?
questions.note: Noun + だって: even.
questions.en: Even he is a human being.

questions.note: It can also mean "but", "even" or "I hear".
それから only means after that, in time.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that means "after that"
questions.note: それから links two events in time.
questions.en: I took a bath, and after that I went to sleep.

questions.note: だから gives the result.
questions.en: It was rainy. So I did not go.

questions.note: Noun + だって: even.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that reports what you heard
questions.note: だって at the end: it is said.
questions.en: I hear Tanaka is off today.

questions.prompt: I hear the teacher is off tomorrow.
questions.note: Plain sentence + だって: hearsay.
questions.en: I hear the teacher is off tomorrow.

questions.prompt: I did my homework, and after that I slept.

questions.note: Noun + だって: even.
